Bayer Akselerasi Regenerasi Petani Indonesia melalui Program SATRIA, Gelar Temu 500 Petani Muda di Magelang
Dengan 66,44% petani Indonesia berusia di atas 45 tahun, Program Bayer SATRIA membekali petani muda dengan teknologi, pembiayaan, akses pasar, dan kapabilitas digital.
Petani muda peserta Program Bayer SATRIA di Magelang
Diskusi lapangan petani muda pada temu SATRIA di Ngablak, Magelang

**MAGELANG, Jawa Tengah, 30 Juni 2026** — Bayer Indonesia menggelar temu **500 petani muda** di Magelang sebagai bagian dari **Program Bayer SATRIA** (Sinergi Petani Muda Mitra Bayer untuk Indonesia) — inisiatif pemberdayaan generasi muda untuk mengembangkan usaha tani yang produktif, menguntungkan, dan berkelanjutan.

Indonesia tengah menghadapi tantangan regenerasi petani: Sensus Pertanian 2023 mencatat 66,44% petani aktif berusia di atas 45 tahun, sementara rasio petani muda hanya 21,93%. Program SATRIA — perluasan strategis dari inisiatif Better Life Farming yang telah mendampingi lebih dari 1,8 juta petani lahan kecil sejak 2020 — dibangun di atas empat pilar: inovasi teknologi pertanian, digital marketing, ekosistem pertanian, dan *agents of change*.

"Regenerasi petani bukan hanya tentang kuantitas, tetapi juga kualitas — yaitu petani muda yang siap, adaptif, dan bangga dengan profesinya," ujar **Maria Magdalena Pakpahan**, Head of BLF Bayer Indonesia.

Dipusatkan di Lapangan Cakra Buana, Kecamatan Ngablak, kegiatan berfokus pada komoditas cabai merah keriting — termasuk pengenalan paket cabai super Bayer yang berpotensi meningkatkan hasil panen sekitar 23%. Petani muda juga mendapat akses fasilitas pembiayaan KUR, jalur pemasaran bersama Indofood, dan pelatihan konten pemasaran digital bersama influencer pertanian.

"Pendampingan Program Bayer SATRIA memberikan manfaat nyata bagi saya — memperkuat kemampuan menerapkan praktik pertanian modern sekaligus membangun jejaring dengan sesama petani," kata **Arum Wulandari**, petani muda dari Desa Banyuroto, Sawangan.

Setelah Padang dan Magelang, Program SATRIA akan berlanjut ke sentra-sentra pertanian lain, termasuk melalui **Bayer SATRIA Campus Challenge** bersama perguruan tinggi terkemuka.

APL Hadirkan Tirzepatide untuk Memperkuat Tatalaksana Penyakit Metabolik di Indonesia

Agonis reseptor ganda GIP/GLP-1 pertama di kelasnya kini tersedia di Indonesia — pilihan terapi baru berbasis bukti untuk diabetes melitus tipe 2 dan obesitas, dengan izin edar BPOM melalui jalur reliance.
Media briefing APL menghadirkan tirzepatide di Jakarta
Narasumber memaparkan tatalaksana penyakit metabolik pada media briefing APL

**JAKARTA, 4 Juli 2026** — PT Anugerah Pharmindo Lestari (APL), sebuah perusahaan Zuellig Pharma, mengumumkan kehadiran **tirzepatide** di Indonesia — agonis reseptor ganda GIP dan GLP-1 pertama di kelasnya, yang menawarkan pilihan terapi baru berbasis bukti untuk penanganan diabetes melitus tipe 2 dan obesitas.

Berdasarkan IDF Diabetes Atlas 2025, diperkirakan 20,4 juta orang dewasa hidup dengan diabetes di Indonesia — diproyeksikan mencapai 28,6 juta pada 2050 — sementara prevalensi obesitas dewasa telah mencapai 23,4%.

"Hadirnya tirzepatide merupakan langkah penting dalam upaya kami menghadirkan inovasi kesehatan yang berdampak bagi masyarakat Indonesia," ujar **Christophe Piganiol**, Presiden Direktur APL.

Kehadiran tirzepatide terwujud berkat kolaborasi erat dengan BPOM, yang menyetujui izin edar dalam 98 hari kerja — serta indikasi manajemen berat badan kronis hanya dalam 42 hari kerja melalui jalur *reliance*. "BPOM berkomitmen untuk terus membangun ekosistem regulasi yang adaptif agar masyarakat Indonesia dapat memperoleh manfaat dari inovasi di bidang kesehatan," ujar **Prof. dr. Taruna Ikrar, M.Biomed., Ph.D.**, Kepala BPOM.

**Prof. Dr. dr. Em Yunir, SpPD-KEMD** (Ketua Umum PERKENI) menjelaskan bahwa berbagai studi klinis menunjukkan tirzepatide mampu memberikan kontrol glikemik signifikan sekaligus penurunan berat badan yang berarti. Sementara **Prof. dr. Dante Saksono Harbuwono, Sp.PD-KEMD, Ph.D.** (Ketua HISOBI) menekankan: "Obesitas adalah masalah perubahan faktor metabolisme tubuh — dengan menurunkan angka obesitas, kita secara langsung dapat menurunkan angka kejadian diabetes, hipertensi, serta risiko penyakit kardiovaskular."

Bayer Indonesia Luncurkan Camalus: Inovasi Insektisida Sistemik Ganda untuk Memperkuat Produktivitas Hortikultura Nasional
Perdana diperkenalkan di Indonesia — negara ketiga secara global setelah India dan Filipina — Camalus mengendalikan hama pengunyah dan penusuk-penghisap sekaligus, di hadapan 350 petani Simalungun.
Peluncuran Camalus di lahan demplot cabai, Simalungun, Sumatra Utara
Tim Bayer dan petani hortikultura pada peluncuran Camalus

**SIMALUNGUN, Sumatra Utara, 6 Juli 2026** — Bayer, perusahaan life science global yang bergerak di bidang kesehatan dan pertanian, meluncurkan **Camalus**, insektisida generasi terbaru untuk petani hortikultura di Indonesia. Camalus merupakan insektisida pertama yang mampu mengendalikan hama pengunyah dan pengisap sekaligus pada tanaman hortikultura — menjawab kebutuhan petani yang selama ini harus mencampur dua insektisida berbeda.

Indonesia menjadi pasar ketiga Camalus secara global, setelah India dan Filipina. Peluncuran di Kabupaten Simalungun dihadiri 350 petani desa setempat, yang menyaksikan langsung efektivitas Camalus di lahan demplot cabai, tomat, dan kubis — tiga komoditas hortikultura andalan wilayah tersebut.

"Tantangan yang dihadapi petani hortikultura semakin kompleks karena hama pengunyah dan penghisap umumnya menyerang bersamaan. Camalus dari Bayer menjawab kesenjangan kebutuhan yang selama ini belum terpenuhi dalam budidaya tanaman hortikultura," ujar **Kukuh Ambar Waluyo**, Head of Field Solutions Bayer South East Asia & Pakistan.

Berbahan aktif Tetraniliprole dan Spirotetramat dengan mekanisme kerja ganda (*dual mode of action*), Camalus bergerak dua arah di dalam jaringan tanaman sehingga memberikan perlindungan menyeluruh — di dalam dan luar daun, batang, buah, hingga tunas baru. Proses riset dan pengembangannya berlangsung sekitar 10 tahun, termasuk ratusan uji coba lapangan di Indonesia dan pengujian intensif di pusat riset Bayer JUARA, Klaten.

"Kami memastikan agar Camalus hadir dekat dengan keseharian petani, baik dari sisi ketersediaan maupun kemudahan akses," ujar **Krisna Dwi Laksono**, Commercial Unit Lead West, Bayer Crop Science Indonesia. Bayer akan memperluas distribusi Camalus ke 13 provinsi sepanjang 2026, melalui jaringan kios tani termasuk Better Life Farming Center.

*Siaran pers ini disusun dan didistribusikan oleh R&R Communications untuk Bayer Indonesia. Media enquiries: contact@rikadanrekan.id.*

Why Earned Media Still Anchors Reputation in Indonesia
Paid reach is easy to buy and easy to ignore. After 100,000 coverage clips, here is why earned media remains the foundation of corporate reputation in Indonesia.

Every year, someone declares the press release dead. Every year, the brands that hold the strongest reputations in Indonesia keep earning coverage — and the numbers keep proving the point.

## Trust is not transferable

Paid media buys attention. Earned media borrows credibility — the journalist's, the publication's, the editor's judgement that this story deserves space. That distinction matters more in Indonesia than in many markets, because Indonesian audiences remain highly attuned to the difference between advertising and news, and because national media still shapes the agenda for regional outlets and social conversation alike.

When a health desk covers a public education campaign, or a technology editor benchmarks a product launch, the coverage carries a signal no ad budget can replicate: *someone independent decided this mattered.*

## The compounding effect

A single placement is a moment. A sustained media programme is an asset. Across our longest retainers — several running for seven years or more — the pattern repeats: coverage compounds. Journalists who covered the first campaign answer the second call faster. Spokespeople who performed well get invited back. The brand becomes a reference point rather than a pitch.

This is why we counsel clients to treat media relations as a programme, not a series of announcements. The 759 articles behind one recent healthcare campaign were not the product of one big moment — they were twelve deliberately sequenced activities, each building on the last.

## What earned media demands in return

Earned coverage has a price, and it is not paid in rupiah. It is paid in:

- **A real story.** Editors are not obliged to care. The angle has to survive contact with a newsroom.
- **Genuine access.** Spokespeople who show up, answer directly, and respect journalists' time.
- **Consistency.** One available quote in a crisis is worth ten press conferences in calm weather — but only if the relationship existed before the crisis.

Brands that pay that price hold reputations that discounting competitors cannot buy. Twenty-six years in, we have yet to see an exception.

Influencer Programmes That Hold Up: Fit Before Followers
After 40,000+ managed creator posts, the lesson is consistent: audience fit and long-term relationships beat follower counts every time.

Indonesia has one of the most active creator economies in the world, and one of the easiest ones to waste money in. The difference between the two usually comes down to decisions made before the first creator is ever contacted.

## Start with mapping, not shopping

The most common mistake in influencer marketing is starting from a list of names. Reach is the last filter to apply, not the first. The questions that actually predict performance:

- Does this creator's audience overlap with the people the brand needs to reach — or just resemble them demographically?
- Has the creator built credibility in this category, or would the endorsement read as a detour?
- Does their content style survive a brand brief, or collapse into an ad read?

Proper mapping answers these before budgets are committed. It is slower than shopping from a rate card. It is also the reason some campaigns produce advocacy and others produce inventory.

## Relationships outperform transactions

A creator posting for a brand the third year running communicates something a one-off post cannot: continuity reads as conviction. This is why our influencer practice is structured around ongoing relations — first approach, relationship management, then campaigns — rather than campaign-by-campaign procurement.

The practical benefits are unglamorous and decisive: better rates, better content, faster turnarounds, and creators who flag problems early because the relationship is worth protecting.

## Measure what the brief asked for

Every influencer campaign should end the way it began — against the brief. Impressions are an output; the brief defined an outcome. Monitoring and evaluation should track sentiment, message pull-through and audience response, not just delivery counts.

More than 40,000 reviewer and influencer posts into this discipline, our conclusion is unchanged: creators are a media channel with feelings. Treat the channel strategically and the people well, and it performs. Reverse the two, and it does not.

Crisis Readiness: What to Have in Place Before You Need It
Crises are won in preparation, not in the moment. Four assets every corporate communications team in Indonesia should have ready before the phone rings.

No organisation plans to have a crisis. Every organisation, eventually, has one. The gap between a difficult week and a lasting reputational wound is usually determined by what existed *before* the story broke.

## 1. A fact base that is already assembled

The first hours of a crisis are consumed by a question that should never need asking: *what do we actually know?* Organisations that maintain a current fact base — operations, safety records, past incidents, regulatory standing — respond in hours. Organisations that must assemble one respond in days, and the story is written without them.

This is why our crisis work begins with problem-based background analysis. The discipline of understanding what is genuinely at stake, done calmly in advance, is worth more than any statement template.

## 2. A decision chain with names on it

"Who approves the statement?" is a fatal question to be asking at midnight. A workable crisis protocol fits on one page: who speaks, who approves, who informs the board, and who is empowered to act when the first three are unreachable. Rehearse it once a year. The rehearsal will feel unnecessary right up until it is not.

## 3. Relationships that predate the crisis

Editors extend the benefit of the doubt to organisations they know. A spokesperson calling a newsroom for the first time during a crisis is a stranger asking for a favour. A spokesperson who has been accessible for years is a known quantity making a request. Media relations in calm periods is crisis insurance — it simply is not labelled that way.

## 4. The discipline of one voice

In a crisis, contradiction is more damaging than bad news. A single, factual, consistently delivered account — updated as facts develop, never ahead of them — outperforms every clever framing. Real-time response management is largely the discipline of keeping an organisation saying one true thing while events tempt it to say several.

None of this removes the difficulty of a genuine crisis. It determines whether the organisation walks out of it with its credibility intact. The time to find out is not the day it happens.

MSD Indonesia and Kemenkes Expand Health Education on HPV Prevention for Boys
Kelas Jurnalis 2026 brings journalists and health authorities together to broaden public understanding of HPV prevention — extending protection beyond girls to the next generation of boys.

**JAKARTA, 22 April 2026** — MSD Indonesia, together with the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Indonesia, convened Kelas Jurnalis 2026, a journalism class dedicated to deepening media understanding of HPV (Human Papillomavirus) prevention in boys — a critical step in broadening national immunization awareness beyond cervical cancer prevention in girls.

The program brought national health journalists together with clinicians and Ministry of Health officials to examine the epidemiology of HPV-related diseases and the role of accurate reporting in public health outcomes.

Kelas Jurnalis continues the education-first partnership between MSD Indonesia and R&R Communications that began in 2022, which has produced the "Tenang untuk Menang" campaign and journalism roadshows reaching key cities across Indonesia.
